newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Indonesia coffee prices up on tight supply.
newsitem.headline: Indonesia coffee prices up on tight supply.

text.p: Indonesian Robusta coffee prices were higher on Monday from a week ago on tight post-harvest supply and sporadic short-covering, traders said.
The local price was quoted at 2,650-2,700 rupiah/kg in the key growing region of Lampung in South Sumatra, compared with 2,600-2,650 rupiah last week.
The export price was $1,210-$1,220/tonne, up from $1,200 a week ago.
"The market is generally quiet because there aren't many beans left after the harvest," one Lampung trader said. "A few players are continuing to cover positions."
Other traders said Indonesian coffee was facing stiff competition from Vietnamese beans, which were being sold at a discount to local coffee.
"I heard that Vietnam is offering at $1,000-$1,110 per tonne. How can we compete with that price?" said one trader.
The trader said there was an estimated 60,000 to 70,000 tonnes of coffee in the hands of farmers and exporters at the moment, compared with 100,000 tonnes at the end of September.
Traders said they expected the next coffee harvest to begin in earnest in late March, although small amounts of beans would begin to flow from as early as January.
